question_papers.paper_title: Set 1 - Magnetic Effects of Electric Current Practice Paper

questions.question_text: Which rule is used to determine the direction of mechanical force acting on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field?
options: Right-Hand Thumb Rule
Fleming's Left-Hand Rule
Fleming's Right-Hand Rule
Ohm's Law
questions.correct_answer: Fleming's Left-Hand Rule

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements correctly describes key observations in Magnetic Effects of Electric Current (Set 1)?
options: Core process in Magnetic Effects of Electric Current obeys conservation laws and standard reaction conditions.
Process in Magnetic Effects of Electric Current violates mass conservation.
No physical or chemical state change occurs during the reaction.
Products have higher total mass than initial reactants.
questions.correct_answer: Core process in Magnetic Effects of Electric Current obeys conservation laws and standard reaction conditions.

questions.question_text: What physical state symbol or indicator color change is associated with Magnetic Effects of Electric Current (Set 1)?
options: Aqueous solution (aq) with characteristic color change
Solid precipitate (s) with gas emission
Gaseous phase (g) only
Liquid phase (l) with zero temperature change
questions.correct_answer: Aqueous solution (aq) with characteristic color change

questions.question_text: Identify the correct SI unit or mathematical relationship relevant to Magnetic Effects of Electric Current (Set 1).
options: Standard NCERT Formula & Unit
Dimensionless Ratio x 100
Inverse Square Exponential
Absolute Constant Zero
questions.correct_answer: Standard NCERT Formula & Unit

questions.question_text:

Reason (R): Molecular and atomic rearrangements preserve total mass, charge, and energy balance.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

A is true but R is false

questions.correct_answer: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

questions.question_text: Explain the role of Earth wire and Safety Fuse in domestic electric circuits.
options: Option A
Option B
Option C
Option D
questions.correct_answer: Earth wire grounds metallic appliance bodies to prevent electric shocks. Fuse wire melts when current exceeds safe limits, breaking the circuit to prevent fires.

questions.question_text: Describe the construction and working principle of an Electric Motor.
options: Option A
Option B
Option C
Option D
questions.correct_answer: Principle: Current-carrying armature coil in a magnetic field experiences a rotational force (Fleming's Left-Hand Rule). Commutator split-rings reverse current direction every half rotation to sustain continuous uni-directional torque.
